fishingbat: A greater bulldog bat in flight over water, both wings spread wide to either side, seen from the front. The animal is shown entirely on its own, isolated, with no other object of any kind in the picture. IT IS A BAT AND ITS HEAD IS A BAT'S HEAD - a small furry pointed bat face with two upright pointed ears standing up on top of its head, a short tapering muzzle and small dark eyes. Its lips are somewhat full and its upper lip is divided by a narrow vertical cleft, and there are loose fleshy folds at the corners of its mouth, but the head stays small, furry and pointed. ITS HIND FEET ARE ENORMOUS, hanging down well below its body on long bare legs and armed with BIG CURVED HOOKED CLAWS for gaffing fish out of the water. Long narrow pointed wings of orange-brown leather. Bright rusty-orange fur
greaterhorseshoebat: A greater horseshoe bat in flight, both wings spread wide to either side, seen from the front so its face is turned straight toward the viewer. The animal is shown entirely on its own, isolated, with no other object of any kind in the picture. THE FACE IS THE WHOLE POINT AND IT IS ELABORATE: a LARGE FLESHY PALE PINK-GREY PLATE OF BARE SKIN COVERS THE ENTIRE FRONT OF ITS FACE like a mask, and that plate is built in three parts - a broad ROUNDED HORSESHOE-SHAPED FLAP, shaped like a letter U lying open at the bottom, wraps right around both nostrils; from the middle of it a small UPRIGHT RIDGE rises; and above that a TALL POINTED TRIANGULAR SPEARHEAD OF SKIN stands straight up between its eyes like the blade of a spade. This whole fleshy structure is big, pale and unmistakable, taking up most of its face. Very large broad pointed ears with no spike inside, small dark eyes almost buried in fur, soft grey-brown fur, broad rounded greyish-brown wing membranes
longnosedbat: A lesser long-nosed bat in flight, hovering with both wings spread wide to either side, seen from the front. The animal is shown entirely on its own, isolated, with no other object of any kind in the picture. ITS MUZZLE IS VERY LONG AND SLENDER, a narrow tapering snout AS LONG AGAIN AS THE REST OF ITS HEAD, projecting far forward like the muzzle of a tiny deer, with a small triangular flap of skin at its tip. A NARROW PINK TONGUE extends forward from the end of that long snout to drink nectar. Cinnamon-brown fur dusted with pale yellow pollen around its face and shoulders, narrow pointed wings, small ears, dark eyes
